notes:
A clean five-bullet Dancer AF page. The one judgement call is the sub-bullet under bullet 1: it is not commentary, it is the whole item hunt -- 'to complete this quest, you must have a Block of Yagudo Glue', and the page explicitly tells you to get it BEFORE bullet 2. So it becomes step 2, an obtain with the five Shadowreign Yagudo as drop mobs and the glue as evidence. Its zone is deliberately nil: the page defers to the Yagudo Glue page for the zone list and only names Castle Oztroja (S) as the fastest, not the only, place, so a pinned zone would be narrower than the page. The item is written 'Block of Yagudo Glue' in Item Reqs and 'Yagudo Glue' in bullet 4; both fold to item 2558 and the long form is used throughout. Bullets 3 and 4 are two separate interactions with the same Glowing Pebbles -- examine for a cutscene, then trade -- and are kept apart because the trade is what consumes the glue; consecutive steps on the same object are one marker anyway. The 'You must be on Dancer' sub-bullets are the job gate restated, not steps. The trailing transclusion of 'Matthias' is the NEXT quest and carries nothing here. Level '50+ Dancer' is both gates. Repeatable 'af' means false.

notes: The header's giver, Gilgamesh in the Hall of the Gods, is never mentioned in the walkthrough -- every action bullet is Joachim in Port Jeuno, and the quest ENDS by zoning into the Hall of the Gods. The start is left where the header put it rather than moved: v1 already marks gilgamesh in zone 251, the Hall of the Gods is genuinely where the last step happens, and moving it to Joachim would be a guess about which end of the quest the flag sits at. Demoted to medium for that gap. Three consecutive Joachim steps are kept separate rather than merged because the page gives them as three distinct conversations; the runtime treats consecutive steps on one NPC as a single marker regardless. ADVERSARY PASS: both Ivory abyssite key items have been struck as evidence. Bullets 1 and 2 read 'Speak to Joachim ... AFTER completing eight/all nine of the following quests AND RECEIVING the Ivory abyssite of prosperity/destiny Key Item' -- the abyssites are preconditions brought in from those other quests, not something these steps hand you, and holding one would have advanced the ladder before the player ever spoke to Joachim. That leaves this quest with no observable at all; the ladder rests entirely on the session latch, which is the second reason for medium. The 8-of-9-then-9-of-9 quest count has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so the nine quests are recorded in the step notes and not as gates.prev: prev is an AND-list and 'eight of these nine' is not. The Previous field's three 'Expansion Set Quests' entries are expansion names, not quest titles, so only A Sea Dog's Summons is carried. The final cutscene is a game-clock window, 18:00 to 5:00, which no packet reports.

notes: Four bullets, four steps, and the page is unambiguous throughout. Bullet 2 and bullet 3 are two examines of the SAME Tiger Bones and are deliberately not merged: the first spawns Old Sabertooth, the second -- only after it has died on its own, roughly three earth minutes later -- hands over the Old tiger's fang, and that key item is the quest's only observable. Old Sabertooth carries role 'spawn' and nothing else on purpose: the page is emphatic that fighting or disturbing it forfeits the key item, so a sword glyph on it would be actively wrong advice. The three-minute wait is a note rather than a `wait` step -- it is unmarkable, unobservable, and would only push a blank rung between two clicks on one object. The Trust chatter about Shikaree Z under bullet 1 is Perih Vashai's unrelated dialogue, not a step. Level 30+ with no job named is the level gate only, so jobs stays empty; becoming a Ranger is the reward.

notes:
This quest has NO giver -- the header's Start field is empty and bullet 1 says outright that it flags on completing Re-Drafted by the Duchy -- which is why v1 dropped it entirely. So start.npc is an honest null and the quest is carried by its steps; anything markable here is a gain over nothing. Bullet 1 is therefore not a step. Bullets 2 and 4 each hold three Voidwatch battles in three different zones, so they become three steps apiece, one zone each, sharing a group because the page states no order between them. Each battle lists three portal coordinates rather than one, so grid stays nil and all three go in the note -- a step has one grid and picking one of three would be a coin flip. The two generic NPCs are treated differently on purpose: 'Atmacite Refiner' is a distinct name and keeps its marker with a nil zone, which is exactly right for 'any refiner'; 'Voidwatch Officer' is on the addon's known-ambiguous list, where a nil zone means 'mark every one in Vana'diel', so that step deliberately drops its target and keeps only its rung and its evidence. The White stratum abyssite V is granted at step 4 and yet is also the header's Reward, so by rule it cannot be evidence -- flagged, because in this quest it demonstrably is NOT the end of the quest and a human may want to overrule that. The Voidwatch alarum at step 8 is the one clean evidence point. 'Audience Chamber' is the page's own name for the palace entrance in Ru'Lude Gardens; if it does not match a live entity the step keeps its place and loses only its marker.

notes: The whole walkthrough is one wikitable cell with '*' and '**' bullets instead of numbered ones; source_bullets number the six '*' items 1..6 in the order they appear, and the '**' lines are all routing advice. Neither end of this quest has an entity: it opens by WALKING toward the Palace in Ru'Lude Gardens and closes by returning to it, and 'the Palace' is a description, not a name -- so both steps are targetless and keep only their zone. The header's giver Esha'ntarl never appears in the walkthrough but stands in that zone, so she is left as the start rather than moved; that is where the only marker this quest can carry will sit. Bullets 3 and 4 are the same Unstable Displacement twice -- approach for a cutscene, then click it again to enter the battlefield -- and are kept apart because only the second one opens the BC. Quest Reqs 'Promathia Mission 8-4' has no schema slot, and the walkthrough's own precondition (all the post-Dawn cutscenes including Blueblade Fell) is likewise unobservable. The reward Whisper of the Wyrmking is the header's Reward, so it is not evidence: this quest has no observable at all, and the ladder rests entirely on the session latch. Demoted to medium for that and for the table.

notes:
Three bullets and all three are real. Bullet 2 reads like routing advice but is the only place the page says where the Tremorstone comes from -- the Cloister of Tremors in the west of the Quicksand Caves -- so it is an obtain step with the Tremorstone as its evidence, and the Unity Warp 125 and Home Point #2 hints stay in the note. Nothing in that cloister is named as a clickable, so the target is nil. The OR branch is the interesting part: the quest wants a Tremorstone AND one of Meteorite / Soil Gem / 12x Soil Geode, and the runtime's alternates are a flat 'items, or any one of items_alt' with no shared mandatory term. Modelled as items = Tremorstone + Meteorite with the other two as alternates, which is the closest expressible shape; items_partial is set because the Tremorstone half of the requirement cannot be carried into the alternates. In practice the ladder does not reach this step until the Tremorstone is already in hand, so the loose alternate costs little. The sub-bullets naming Crawlers on Starfall Hillock, Colonization Reives, Mog Gardens and Goldsmithing are sources for the alternates, not steps. Reward [KI] Loadstone is a reward, not evidence -- it is what makes the Quicksand Caves weighted doors soloable, which is why Crying Over Onions points here.
